overview.title: What is 'Community' and Why Is It Important?
overview.knowledge_focus: Students develop an understanding of community as a shared identity-forming narrative and explore how communities influence belonging, identity, and worldview.
overview.skill_focus: Determine and summarize the central idea of a text and identify details that develop it.

objectives.statement: Students will determine the central idea of the text and explain how it is developed through supporting details.
Students will explain how communities shape identity and belonging using evidence from the text.
Students will summarize the author's definition of community in their own words.
Students will interpret vocabulary and word meaning in context.

key_term.definition: A group of people who share an identity-forming narrative.
A feeling of unity or togetherness based on a common interest.
A sign or example of something becoming visible.
The quality that makes something what it is.
A story or account that shapes understanding or identity.
Related to standards of behavior or ideas about what is right and wrong.

phases.title: Lesson Introduction
phases.activity: Teacher guides students through the slide deck introducing the concept of community and the lesson skill focus.

phases.title: Guided Reading and Discussion
phases.activity: Students read the article and answer During Reading Questions focused on central idea, supporting details, and definition of community.

phases.title: Community Reflection
phases.activity: Students discuss communities they belong to and explain how those communities fit Lowe’s definition.

phases.title: Independent Assessment
phases.activity: Students complete multiple-choice questions and a short written response explaining the author's definition of community.

phases.title: Student-Led Discussion
phases.activity: Students discuss courteous behavior, conformity, and benefits of belonging to multiple communities.

formative_checks.question: Which best describes the author’s main purpose in writing the article?
options: to illustrate how important it is to be part of multiple communities
to demonstrate the way community has shaped the author's life
to describe the life of a person who lives in Newcastle
to give a clear and useful definition of community

formative_checks.question: Which piece of evidence best illustrates the central idea of the article?
options: One of the communities that I consider myself to be part of is the community based around the city of Newcastle.
It is this choice to participate in the making and remaking of these stories about the city that makes me part of the community of Newcastle.
Community is a group of people who share a story that is so important to them that it defines an aspect of who they are.
Social change requires that we rewrite our communal narratives.

formative_checks.question: What is the best meaning of the word 'slighted' as it is used in paragraph 5?
How do paragraphs 5-7 help the reader understand the author’s central idea?
options: by explaining why community is neither good nor bad
by describing life for members of the Newcastle community
by giving an example of a community that is part of the author’s story
by illustrating how the Newcastle community has many different members

formative_checks.question: Explain what Lowe means when he says a community is 'a group of people who share an identity-forming narrative.'
